statement: For a Newman polynomial f(z) = sum_{a in A} z^a with A a set of n non-negative integers (coefficients 0/1), let M(A) = min over |z|=1 of |f(z)|. A HIT is an n-term A whose certified lower bound on M(A)^2 strictly exceeds bar(n)^2, where bar(n) is the largest certified M over all anchors with FEWER than n terms — i.e. a Newman polynomial that beats everything achievable with fewer terms. The certificate is an exact enclosure of the global minimum of |f|^2 = n + 2*sum_{i<j} cos((a_j-a_i)theta), reduced to a global minimum of an integer-coefficient polynomial on [-1,1] via cos(d*theta) = T_d(cos theta) and certified by Sturm isolation plus interval-Newton refinement with exact rational value enclosures (instruments/trigmin). bar(n) is COMPUTED from pinned witness exponent sets at load time, never transcribed. A separate TRIPWIRE flags any certified M >= 2 carried by at most 18 terms, which would improve the certified record that the least n with mu(n) >= 2 is at most 19; a tripwire is a flag for the owner and is never a result.
